PRENATAL GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
MRN: [redacted ID]
Referring Physician: Dr. [redacted name]
Date of Collection: [redacted date]
Date of Report: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Amniocentesis for prenatal chromosomal abnormality screening

SPECIMEN
Amniotic fluid (20 mL)
Fetal cells from uncultured amniocytes

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR)
Rapid aneuploidy screening for chromosomes 13, 18, and 21

METHODOLOGY
DNA was extracted from uncultured amniocytes. QF-PCR analysis was performed using fluorescently labeled primers for short tandem repeat (STR) markers on chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. A minimum of 4 informative markers per chromosome were analyzed. Peak area ratios were calculated to determine chromosome copy number.

RESULTS

Chromosome 13 STR markers:
D13S631: 1:1 ratio (normal diallelic pattern)
D13S258: 1:1 ratio (normal diallelic pattern)
D13S742: 1:1 ratio (normal diallelic pattern)
D13S628: 1:1 ratio (normal diallelic pattern)

Chromosome 18 STR markers:
D18S391: 1:1 ratio (normal diallelic pattern)
D18S390: 1:1 ratio (normal diallelic pattern)
D18S535: 1:1 ratio (normal diallelic pattern)
D18S386: 1:1 ratio (normal diallelic pattern)

Chromosome 21 STR markers:
D21S1411: 1:1 ratio (normal diallelic pattern)
D21S1412: 1:1 ratio (normal diallelic pattern)
D21S1435: 1:1 ratio (normal diallelic pattern)
D21S1446: 1:1 ratio (normal diallelic pattern)

INTERPRETATION
Normal complement for chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. No abnormality detected.

No evidence of trisomy 13 (Patau syndrome), trisomy 18 (Edwards syndrome), or trisomy 21 (Down syndrome) in this fetal sample.

LIMITATIONS
This test screens only for common aneuploidies of chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. It does not detect balanced chromosomal rearrangements, mosaicism below 20%, or abnormalities of other chromosomes.

RECOMMENDATIONS
Full karyotype analysis from cultured amniocytes to follow. This will provide comprehensive chromosomal analysis including detection of structural abnormalities and aneuploidies of all chromosomes.

Reported by: [redacted name], Clinical Scientist
Authorized by: Dr. [redacted name], Consultant Clinical Geneticist
